alerts.title: Assam floods: rehab kits reaching worst-hit villages as waters recede in Upper Assam
alerts.summary: Weeks of catastrophic monsoon flooding across Upper Assam — worst in Sivasagar, Nazira, Charaideo and Jorhat districts — killed over 100 people and displaced roughly 700,000. As of August 31 the first batch of rehabilitation kits was being distributed at a local Naamghar in Rudrasagar, Sivasagar, marking a shift from emergency relief to rehabilitation, though around 119,000 hectares of cropland remain submerged and some pockets are still awaiting coverage.
alerts.impact: Serviceability recovering but fragile — Upper Assam (Sivasagar/Nazira/Charaideo/Jorhat): keep a light NS watch on flood-hit pincodes as roads and bridges are still being repaired; resume normal manifestation gradually and coordinate with Delhivery/Xpressbees on NE routing around the Guwahati hub as access improves.

alerts.title: Assam: fresh Brahmaputra riverbank erosion at Tingkhong's Mohanaghat in Dibrugarh, CM engages IIT-Guwahati
alerts.summary: Fresh riverbank erosion by the Brahmaputra has hit the Mohanaghat area near Tingkhong Bhoga Ali in Dibrugarh district, the latest in a string of erosion incidents this monsoon across Chabua, Balijan, Pukhurijan, Dinjan and Rahmoria that Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma toured on August 2. The state government has now engaged IIT-Guwahati to design a long-term erosion-control solution for the Brahmaputra basin.
alerts.impact: Watch list — Dibrugarh belt (Tingkhong, Chabua, Dinjan, Rahmoria): flag riverside pincodes as erosion-risk, expect gradual land loss to keep some approach roads unstable through the monsoon; no full stoppage yet but build in extra transit time for last-mile in these panchayats.

alerts.title: Himachal Pradesh: Kiratpur-Manali highway blocked again near Banala, 2,000+ vehicles stranded, 287 roads shut statewide
alerts.summary: The Kiratpur-Manali National Highway has been blocked again by multiple fresh landslides between Mandi and Banala, stranding over 2,000 vehicles including tourist traffic across Mandi and Kullu districts. The Kataula alternate diversion route has also failed after a fresh landslide blocked it too, completely snapping road connectivity between Mandi and Kullu. Statewide, 287 roads including major highways remain blocked, cutting off essential-services access to Kullu-Manali and Lahaul-Spiti.
alerts.impact: Critical serviceability risk — Mandi/Kullu/Manali/Lahaul-Spiti corridor: hold non-time-critical linehaul on this NH, there is currently no reliable diversion (both Kataula and earlier Nauni Chowk routes have failed at various points), and keep 5+ day buffer stock at Mandi/Kullu hubs given repeated closures this month. Flag Lahaul-Spiti pincodes as at serviceability risk until connectivity is restored.

alerts.title: Manipur: NH202 Imphal-Ukhrul road still in deplorable condition, Kamjong bailey bridge unrepaired since July
alerts.summary: The August flash floods and landslides across Senapati, Ukhrul and Kamjong hill districts washed away roads, farmland and bridges, and NH202 (Imphal-Ukhrul road) remains in deplorable, monsoon-battered condition with persistent roadblocks stranding vehicles. The Bailey bridge over the Namban/Nambalok river in Kamjong district — the only link for Chatric and 12 neighbouring border villages — has still not been repaired since it was destroyed in a suspected explosive attack in July.
alerts.impact: Serviceability loss — Ukhrul/Kamjong/Senapati pincodes: keep border villages served via the Kamjong bridge flagged non-serviceable, route Imphal-hub linehaul with extra transit buffer on NH202, and monitor for continued non-adherence in this hill-district LM belt through the monsoon.

alerts.title: Sikkim: NH10 reopens one-way at Bardang/20th Mile after 1.5-month closure; West Sikkim's Gyalshing-Legship route still cut
alerts.summary: NH10 connectivity through the Bardang (20th Mile) stretch on the Singtam-Rangpo link has reopened to one-way vehicular traffic after being closed for roughly 1.5 months following the original July 13 landslide; traffic police are managing one-way movement while restoration continues. Separately, the Gyalshing-Legship route in West Sikkim remains cut off by landslides, and NHIDCL has proposed four tunnels on the Rangpo-Singtam stretch as a long-term fix.
alerts.impact: Watch list, easing — East Sikkim (Singtam-Rangpo): linehaul can resume via the one-way-managed Bardang stretch but keep buffer time for traffic-police-controlled movement; West Sikkim (Gyalshing-Legship) pincodes remain at serviceability risk — continue routing via Silguri-Duga-Rangpo diversion and pre-position buffer stock at the Siliguri gateway hub.

alerts.title: Gujarat: flood-like situation in Anand and Surat after 300mm+ rain in 24 hours, 4 dead, 154 houses damaged
alerts.summary: Extreme rainfall driven by a land-based deep depression pulling moisture from both the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea has created a flood-like situation in Anand and Surat and other south Gujarat districts. Anand recorded the highest rainfall at 320mm and Surat 300mm in 24 hours; 4 deaths and 2 injuries have been reported along with 154 houses damaged. Moderate thunderstorms and heavy rain remain likely at isolated places in Anand, Kheda and Surat.
alerts.impact: Serviceability risk — Surat/Kheda/Anand belt: flag flood-prone pincodes non-serviceable while the alert holds, pre-position buffer stock at the Ahmedabad/Vadodara hubs, and coordinate with Delhivery/Shadowfax on alternate routing around waterlogged stretches in these three districts.

alerts.title: Kerala: monsoon eases to yellow alert but fresh widespread rain spell expected Sep 2-4, Idukki hill belt still fragile
alerts.summary: After orange alerts for Idukki, Wayanad, Palakkad, Malappuram, Kozhikode and Kannur through August 28-29, IMD forecasts isolated-to-scattered rain for Kerala and Lakshadweep on September 1, with fairly widespread to widespread rainfall expected during September 2-4 before easing again September 5-6. The hill districts, especially Idukki, remain sensitive after earlier August landslides.
alerts.impact: Watch list — Idukki/Wayanad/Malappuram/Kottayam hill and highland pincodes: pre-build 2-3 day buffer stock ahead of the September 2-4 rain spell, monitor for fresh landslide-triggered village cutoffs given this belt's monsoon history, and be ready to flag NS for hill-taluka pincodes if alerts are upgraded again.

alerts.title: Bay of Bengal low-pressure system tracks inland toward Jharkhand/Bihar/east MP; Odisha red alert eases, no cyclone forming
alerts.summary: The system that formed near the West Bengal-north Odisha coast in late August consolidated into a well-marked low-pressure area over Gangetic West Bengal and adjoining north coastal Odisha; IMD has ruled out cyclone formation and expects it to move west-northwestwards across Odisha, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh over the next two days, with intense weather activity shifting to east Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and Jharkhand by September 2-3. Mayurbhanj, Balasore and Kendrapara saw red-alert extremely heavy rainfall through August 31 with squally coastal winds of 40-60 kmph.
alerts.impact: Route watch, shifting inland — Balasore/Bhadrak/coastal Odisha and South Bengal hubs can stand down from red-alert posture; instead pre-position buffer stock at Jharkhand (Ranchi/Jamshedpur) and Bihar (Patna) hubs ahead of the September 2-3 heavy-rain window, and monitor east MP hubs for the same system.

alerts.title: Petrol/diesel hold steady Sep 1; commercial 19kg LPG cylinder up ₹9.50-11.50 in second straight monthly hike
alerts.summary: Retail petrol and diesel prices remained unchanged on September 1 across major cities — Delhi ₹102.12/₹95.20, Mumbai ₹111.21/₹97.83, Hyderabad ₹115.69/₹103.82 (petrol/diesel per litre). Commercial 19kg LPG cylinders were hiked by ₹9.50-11.50 depending on city effective September 1 — the second straight monthly increase, mainly affecting restaurants, hotels and eateries — while domestic 14.2kg LPG and CNG/PNG rates stayed unchanged.
alerts.impact: Cost watch, no action yet: no immediate LM/FM disruption. Track weekly for early signal on Delhivery/Shadowfax/Xpressbees fuel-surcharge asks — sustained commercial LPG and crude cost pressure keeps margin pressure building ahead of the next OMC pricing cycle.

alerts.title: Rajasthan: 30+ villages submerged in Sawai Madhopur, Kota-Jaipur and Kota-MP highways underwater
alerts.summary: Torrential rain has created a flood-like situation across eight Rajasthan districts, with Kota, Sawai Madhopur, Tonk and Bundi worst hit. In Sawai Madhopur, dam-released water has submerged the villages of Surwal, Dhanoli, Gogor, Jadavata, Sesha and Machhipura, with residents sheltering on rooftops for two to three days; more than 30 villages are cut off from the main city. Two women have died in rain-related incidents, and Army, NDRF and SDRF teams are conducting rescue operations.
alerts.impact: Serviceability loss — Sawai Madhopur/Kota/Bundi/Tonk belt: flag Surwal, Dhanoli, Gogor, Jadavata, Sesha and Machhipura and other submerged villages non-serviceable, the Kota-Jaipur road and the Rajasthan-MP highway are underwater so hold linehaul via these routes, and monitor rail-linked hubs at Sawai Madhopur station for continued waterlogging disruption.

alerts.title: Bihar: rising Ganga triggers erosion in Danapur and Bhagalpur belt, 10 districts under flood threat
alerts.summary: Rising Ganga water levels have triggered erosion at multiple locations in Danapur, threatening life, property and connectivity; the administration has arranged boats where road access has been cut. In Bhagalpur's Sabour, Kahalgaon and Pirpainti, Ganga erosion is eating into agricultural land, while floodwaters have entered villages in Bariyarpur, Munger. Ten districts — Buxar, Bhojpur, Patna, Vaishali, Samastipur, Munger, Begusarai, Katihar, Bhagalpur and Khagaria — are under imminent flood threat.
alerts.impact: Watch list, river-erosion belt — Danapur (Patna), Sabour/Kahalgaon/Pirpainti (Bhagalpur), Bariyarpur (Munger): flag riverside pincodes as erosion/flood risk, coordinate ferry-dependent last-mile in cut-off pockets, and keep buffer stock at Patna hub given 10 districts are on flood watch.
